title: My English Book 7
header: Builds "My English Book 7" – seventh-grade English syllabus – A4 portrait.
csub: Present Perfect • If • too / enough • who / which • Stories
noteP: هٰذَا الكِتَابُ يُكْمِلُ تَعْلِيمَ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ: المُضَارِعُ التَّامُّ (have / has)، وَالجُمَلُ الشَّرْطِيَّةُ (If … will)، وَ too وَ enough، وَالأَسْمَاءُ المَوْصُولَةُ (who / which / where)، وَالمَاضِي المُسْتَمِرُّ، وَ How much / How many، مَعَ قِصَّتَيْنِ 🇬🇧
noteLi: فِي كُلِّ دَرْسٍ وَرَقَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ لِيَكْتُبَ طِفْلُكُمْ جُمْلَةً إِنْجِلِيزِيَّةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ.
اسْأَلُوهُ: Have you ever …? وَشَجِّعُوهُ عَلَى الإِجَابَةِ.
العَبُوا مَعَهُ: If it rains, … وَيُكْمِلُ الجُمْلَةَ.
الكِتَابُ يُقْرَأُ مِنَ اليَسَارِ إِلَى اليَمِينِ.
blurb: A complete 3D English book with a brand-new design – part 7, with Arabic meanings for every word.
blurbLi: Present perfect: have / has and “Have you ever …?”
who, which, where and the past continuous
How much / How many, and two short stories

units.title: Present Perfect
units.intro: We use have / has + past participle for experiences and for actions that are finished.
items: My father has visited Makkah many times.
I have eaten dates from Madinah.
Have you ever travelled by plane?
No, I have never travelled by plane.

units.title: If … will
units.intro: We use If + present, … will + verb, to talk about real possibilities in the future.
items: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If you study hard, you will pass the test.
If I am hungry, I will eat a sandwich.

acts.title: Choose the right word
rows: If it ... sunny, we will go to the beach.
If you water the plant, it ... grow.
If she ... late, she will miss the bus.
If we hurry, we ... catch the train.

acts.title: Choose the best ending
rows: If you eat too many sweets, ...
I will give it to the police.
I will swim in the sea.

units.title: too & enough
units.intro: too + adjective means more than we want. adjective + enough means as much as we need.
items: The soup is too hot to eat.
These shoes are too small for me.
Omar is old enough to ride a bike.

acts.title: too or enough?
rows: The box is ... heavy to carry.
Is the water warm ... to swim?
I can't reach the shelf. I'm not tall ...

acts.title: Choose the sentence
rows: I can put all my books in this bag.
I can't drink the milk. It's very hot.
We can't play outside. It's very cold.

units.title: who, which & where
units.intro: We use who for people, which for things and animals, and where for places.
items: A doctor is a person who helps sick people.
A teacher is a person who teaches.
A pencil is a thing which we use to write.
A cow is an animal which gives us milk.
A library is a place where we borrow books.
A bakery is a place where we buy bread.

acts.title: who, which or where?
rows: A pilot is a person ... flies planes.
A fridge is a machine ... keeps food cold.
A hospital is a place ... doctors work.
A farmer is a person ... grows food.

acts.title: Choose the right ending
rows: A bee is an insect which makes ...
A chef is a person who ...
A school is a place where we ...
Scissors are a tool which we use to ...

units.title: Past Continuous
units.intro: We use was / were + verb-ing for an action that was in progress in the past.
items: I was reading a book at eight o'clock last night.
The boys were playing football in the park.
I was eating lunch when the phone rang.
She was sleeping when I came.

acts.title: Complete the sentence
rows: At seven o'clock, Ali was ... breakfast.
They were ... to school when it started to rain.
What were you ... yesterday at five?
She was reading ... the lights went out.

units.title: How Much? How Many?
units.intro: We use How many with things we can count, and How much with things we cannot count.
items: How many apples are there? There are five apples.
How many books do you have?
How much milk is in the glass? There is a little milk.
How much water do you drink?
We have a lot of dates and a lot of rice.
a lot of friends, a lot of water

acts.title: much or many?
rows: How ... sugar is in the tea?
How ... students are in your class?

acts.title: Choose the answer
rows: How many legs does a spider have?
How much water should we drink?
How many days are there in a week?

units.title: Reading Time
units.intro: Read the stories, then answer the questions.

acts.title: The Best Gift
acts.html:
The Best Gift 🎁

Last week, Hamza was walking home when he saw an old man.
The old man was carrying a heavy bag.
Hamza helped him and carried the bag to his house.
The old man smiled and said, “You have given me the best gift: your kindness.”
Since that day, Hamza has helped many people.

acts.title: Answer
rows: What was Hamza doing when he saw the old man?
What was the old man carrying?
Has Hamza helped other people since that day?

acts.title: Saving Water
acts.html:
Saving Water 💧

Sara saw that the tap in the school garden was dripping.
She thought, “If we don't fix it, we will waste a lot of water.”
She told her teacher, and the teacher called the caretaker.
He fixed the tap the same day.
Sara was happy because she helped to save water.
